description.value: The study investigated structural brain alterations associated with cancer-related PTSD in breast cancer survivors and examined the longitudinal course of gray matter volume over a 2-year follow-up.

design.value: A baseline and 2-year follow-up structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry, with cross-sectional comparisons of breast cancer survivors with PTSD, survivors without PTSD, and healthy subjects, plus longitudinal analyses of the interaction between diagnosis and measurement time.

description.value: A self-reported questionnaire consisting of 15 items: 7 items assessing intrusion symptoms and 8 items assessing avoidance symptoms. Each item is rated using a 4-point scale (“not at all” = 0, “rarely” = 1, “sometimes” = 3, “often” = 5).

task_description.value: Structural brain MRI scans were obtained at baseline and 2 years later. Voxel-based morphometry was used to compare gray matter volume throughout the brain and to examine longitudinal changes within a right BA11 region of interest.

instrument.value: Signa Scanner; GE Medical Systems, Milwaukee, Wisconsin

description.value: MRI scans were performed using a 1.5-T MRI unit with three-dimensional spoiled gradient-recalled acquisition of 1.5-mm contiguous sections under the following conditions: field of view = 230 mm, matrix = 256 × 256 pixels, repetition time (TR) = 25 ms, echo time (TE) = 5 ms, and flip angle = 45°.
VBM was performed using an optimized method with a customized study-specific template set, spatial normalization, tissue segmentation, modulation, and Gaussian smoothing.

steps.value: An optimized study-specific template set consisting of a T1 image and a priori gray, white, and cerebrospinal fluid images was created from brain scans taken from all study subjects.
All scans were spatially normalized to the customized template.
The normalized scans were smoothed with an 8-mm full-width at half-maximum smoothing kernel and averaged to create a customized template.
Images were segmented into gray matter and white matter using customized prior probability maps.
The segments were modulated to correct for volume changes occurring during spatial normalization.
The images were smoothed using a 12-mm full-width at half-maximum Gaussian kernel.
For the amygdala and hippocampus, 4-mm full-width at half-maximum smoothing was performed.

model_settings.value: Baseline gray matter volume differences were analyzed using an ANCOVA with a basic SPM2 model and age, accumulated alcohol consumption, and total gray matter volume as nuisance variables. Significance was set at p = 0.05 corrected using the false discovery rate in regions without a hypothesis; in hypothesized amygdala, hippocampus, ACC, and OFC regions, significance was set at uncorrected p = 0.001 and k = 100. A small volume correction was applied to the bilateral ACC and OFC.

Regional brain volume was correlated with the IES score while controlling for age, accumulated alcohol consumption, and total gray matter volume. The β-value of the brain area within the ROI was extracted using the MarsBaR ROI analysis toolbox. The ROI was set within areas detected to be significantly smaller in cancer survivors with PTSD than in those without PTSD at baseline. Significance was set at p < 0.05, two-tailed.

model_type.value: repeated measures mixed model analysis of covariance

model_settings.value: TIME, DIAGNOSIS, and TIME × DIAGNOSIS were used as effects on brain volume within the ROI. Age, accumulated alcohol consumption, total gray matter volume at baseline, and days from baseline to follow-up were included as covariates. The analysis was performed for the right BA11 gray matter volume in the 76 participants with follow-up data.
Demographic factors were compared to confirm homogeneity between the groups. Significance levels were set at p < 0.05, two-tailed.
